extracted.intended_audience: interested members of the public, regulated entities, state/local/tribal governments, and DOT staff preparing or tracking rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and publication of the Department of Transportation's Semiannual Regulatory Agenda (Unified Agenda) summarizing current and projected rulemakings, reviews of existing regulations, and completed rulemaking actions to inform the public and solicit participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and content of the Regulatory Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Agenda is a semiannual summary of all current and projected rulemakings, reviews of existing regulations, and completed rulemaking actions of the Department of Transportation (DOT). The Regulatory Agenda provides the public with information about DOT's planned regulatory activity for the next 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information should enable public awareness and more effective public participation. Publication in the Federal Register does not impose a binding obligation on the Department and regulatory action beyond items listed is not precluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of public comments and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The public is encouraged to submit comments on any aspect of the Regulatory Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are time-limited (see DATES). To improve the Agenda, the Department solicits suggestions for how it could be further improved. Most documents are available via Regulations.gov and individuals should contact the person listed with each regulation to obtain copies of specific regulatory documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of each Regulatory Agenda entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item in the Regulatory Agenda should include key metadata and descriptive elements such as the agency, title, regulation identifier number (RIN), agency/docket number, CFR parts affected, legal authority, abstract, timetable, regulatory flexibility analysis status, agency contact, and publication citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document Headings may contain the agency or agencies that issued the document; the CFR title and number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number/internal file number; and the RIN which identifies each regulatory action. See the Document Drafting Handbook for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement for agenda items
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rulemaking entry should include an abstract summarizing the rule's purpose, scope, statutory mandates, and intended effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts in the Agenda explain the rule's aim (for example, defining terms, clarifying obligations, adding specific requirements) and note statutory mandates or related merged rulemakings when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable and action chronology
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda entries must present a timetable listing actions (e.g., ANPRM, NPRM, Comment Period End, Final Rule, Interim Final Rule) with corresponding dates and Federal Register citations where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timetables show past actions, comment period dates, next actions, FR cites, and may indicate 'Next Action Undetermined' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry should identify the legal authority (statutes and public laws) under which the rulemaking is being undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal Authority lists relevant U.S.C. sections, public laws, or other statutory references that grant the agency authority to pursue the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each regulation entry must provide an agency contact including name, office, mailing address, phone, fax (if applicable), and email for inquiries and comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information is the point of contact for general comments or item-specific inquiries; the Agenda also notes a central contact for general Regulatory Agenda comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) review notation and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda entries must indicate whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required for the action and discuss RFA-related review activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOT states it regularly reviews existing regulations under the RFA and Executive Orders (e.g., EO 12866, EO 13563), is interested in submissions about requirements that have a 'significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities,' and that operating administrations divide rules into groups for annual analysis and report results in the Fall Agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 610 review and special review notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, entries should note if the action is a Section 610 review or similar statutorily-required review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 610 reviews (Regulatory Flexibility Act) and other mandated reviews should be labeled (e.g., '(Section 610 Review)') in the title/abstract to indicate the type of review being completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with State, Local, and Tribal governments
rubrics_metrics.description: For regulations that have federalism or tribal implications, the Department must develop a process to ensure 'meaningful and timely input' by State, local, and Tribal officials in developing regulatory policies, per Executive Orders 13132 and 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agenda encourages State and local Governments or Indian Tribes to provide information about how DOT rulemakings impact them and to submit input when regulations have 'substantial direct effects' on these entities or on distribution of power and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging and identifying significant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agenda identifies DOT-designated significant regulations with markers (e.g., +, ++) to denote significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table of contents and individual entries show these symbols (e.g., '+ DOT-designated significant regulation') so readers can quickly identify items of heightened significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and authoritative source disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: The online Agenda and XML renditions are an unofficial informational resource; the official legal edition remains the printed Federal Register and the official PDF on govinfo.gov until ACFR grants official status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users relying on the site for legal research should verify results against an official edition. The Agenda notes that the XML-based site does not provide legal notice or judicial notice until official status is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing and related documents linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agenda uses docket IDs and related document lists to link to supporting and related documents (e.g., related Federal Register documents, Regulations.gov entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FederalRegister.gov displays related documents using agency dockets and provides links to PDFs, XML, JSON, MODS metadata, and to Regulations.gov for additional context; supporting documents may or may not be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and editorial guidance (Document Headings and drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings and internal navigation are processed from the legal text and may include a standard set of headings (AGENCY, ACTION, SUMMARY, FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION) and navigational table of contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page advises seeing the Document Drafting Handbook for more details, and notes that the navigational table of contents is a tool with no substantive legal effect.
